Product : Credit Card Issue : Billing Dispute Investigation Complaint I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau review Citibanks handling of my billing dispute concerning defective merchandise purchased with my Citibank credit card. This complaint is not about whether I authorized the purchase. I acknowledge that I made the purchase and that the charge itself is valid. This complaint concerns whether Citibank conducted a reasonable investigation into my dispute involving defective merchandise that failed to perform its intended function as advertised, and whether Citibank fairly considered all relevant evidence before denying my claim. Background On XX/XX/year>, I purchased a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for {$6900.00}. The printer was delivered on XX/XX/year>. Because the equipment required assembly, stand installation, software installation, ink and film loading, and printer configuration before operation, setup took several days to complete. The printers first production print occurred on XX/XX/year>. During its first operational use, the printer failed to perform as intended. The XXXX XXXX transfer would not properly release from the B-film or adhere correctly to multiple application surfaces, resulting in unusable finished products. The defect was discovered during the printers initial operational use. Extensive Efforts to Resolve the Problem Before requesting a refund or filing a dispute, I made every reasonable effort to work directly with the merchant to resolve the issue. Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, I participated in numerous troubleshooting sessions with XXXX technical support team. These efforts included : Multiple remote access sessions in which XXXX technicians connected directly to my computer. Numerous adjustments to printer settings by XXXX technicians. Submission of photographs and videos demonstrating the defect. A final troubleshooting session lasting approximately XXXX hours. Despite these extensive efforts, the printer never produced a usable result. Only after these troubleshooting efforts failed did I request authorization to return the printer for a full refund. This was not buyers remorse or a change of mind. I invested significant time attempting to make the printer function before requesting authorization to return it. Merchant Admissions On XX/XX/year>, XXXX acknowledged in writing : The B-film adhesion/release issue you are experiencing is not a known problem reported by other users, indicating that the problem exists only in your device and is not a systemic issue with the printer model itself. In the same communication, XXXX further acknowledged : You have conducted extensive remote troubleshooting with our technical team, and unfortunately, these efforts have not been able to resolve your issue. These written admissions establish that : XXXX knew exactly what defect was being reported. XXXX acknowledged the issue appeared unique to my specific printer. XXXX acknowledged that extensive troubleshooting had already occurred. XXXX acknowledged that those troubleshooting efforts had failed. Return Request After troubleshooting proved unsuccessful, I requested authorization to return the defective printer for a full refund. A return for a full refund was never authorized. Instead, XXXX repeatedly requested additional troubleshooting. Months later, after Citibank contacted XXXX regarding my dispute, XXXX suggested that I ship the printer back. However, XXXX did not commit in writing to : providing a full refund ; paying return shipping ; specifying inspection timeframes ; or explaining the conditions under which a refund would actually be issued. Had XXXX accepted the return of the defective printer for a full refund when requested, this dispute would never have been necessary. Concerns Regarding Citibanks Investigation Throughout the dispute process, I submitted documentation including : a detailed timeline, photographs demonstrating the defect, merchant correspondence, documentation of extensive troubleshooting, and XXXX written acknowledgements regarding the defect. I also emailed video evidence showing the printers failure during troubleshooting. After being told the videos could not be opened, I asked how that evidence could be submitted, but I did not receive instructions for submitting the videos. Despite this documentation, Citibank denied the dispute. The denial letters raise several concerns. One determination stated that Citibank was unable to identify or determine that a billing error had occurred. When I questioned that determination, Citibank acknowledged that the dispute had been coded incorrectly and reopened the dispute. The second denial stated that I had possessed the merchandise for an extended period before discovering the defect. However, the documented timeline shows : XX/XX/XXXX XXXX received. XX/XX/XXXX First operational use. XX/XX/XXXX Defect discovered during first use. XX/XX/XXXX Return requested after multiple unsuccessful troubleshooting sessions. Additionally, Citibanks XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> determination states : We have investigated your dispute involving a service ( s ) which was not performed. Since the merchant was willing to provide the service ( s ), we are unable to assist you further. My dispute did not involve services that were not performed. My dispute concerned defective merchandise that failed to perform its intended function as advertised. This language raises a concern that the dispute may not have been investigated under the correct dispute category. Request for CFPB Review I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether Citibank conducted a reasonable investigation by determining : Whether the dispute was investigated under the correct dispute category. Whether Citibank considered the complete timeline demonstrating that the defect was discovered during the printers first operational use. Whether Citibank considered XXXX written admissions acknowledging both the defect and unsuccessful troubleshooting. Whether Citibank evaluated whether XXXX ever actually offered to accept the return of the printer for a full refund. Whether Citibanks conclusions were supported by the evidence contained within the dispute file. I am not asking the CFPB to determine whether the printer is defective. Rather, I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether Citibank fulfilled its obligation to conduct a fair, complete, and reasonable investigation of my billing dispute.

complaint_text: To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to formally complain about the handling of a {$32000.00} check deposit and the continued freeze on my accounts and online access, now going into its fourth day. For context : I have been a Wells Fargo customer for 19 years, since this bank was XXXX, and have banked at my local branch for over a decade. On Wednesday, XX/XX/2026, I deposited a {$32000.00} check - proceeds from the sale of a company where I was an equity partner, drawn on another Wells Fargo account. On Thursday, XX/XX/XXXX, the funds were made available in my account. Relying on that availability, I made a Roth IRA contribution and paid several expenses and debts. On Friday, XX/XX/XXXX, I woke up to a checking account balance of approximately - {$12000.00}, with no prior notice, and an email from your Loss Prevention team stating that my checking and savings accounts could be closed. Since then, my accounts have not actually been closed, but deposits have been frozen and I have been completely locked out of online access. It is now Monday, XX/XX/XXXX, and I still do not have online access, with no clear timeline for restoration. When I called Loss Prevention on Saturday, I was told my online access could not be restored because the check still needed to be validated. This does not add up : the funds had already been returned to my account by that point, which means the check had evidently already been treated as valid. Nobody I've spoken with has been able to give me a clear or consistent explanation. The one person who has been genuinely helpful throughout this is XXXX XXXX, Senior Branch Premier Banker at my local branch ( NMLS ID : XXXX ). I would ask that this matter be coordinated with her directly, as she is the only point of contact who has taken the time to understand the situation. What I requested : 1. A clear, specific explanation of what occurred with this check and why funds were reversed after being made available. 2. Immediate restoration of my online banking access and deposit capability. 3. Confirmation that no further negative action ( fees, closure, credit reporting ) will result from this, given the transaction was legitimate and between two Wells Fargo accounts. 4. A direct line of communication with someone able to actually resolve this ideally in coordination with XXXX XXXX rather than a general Loss Prevention queue. This has now cost me four full business days without normal access to my own accounts, on funds your bank itself made available. I expect a prompt, substantive response.Frankly, after 19 years of loyalty to this bank, this experience has left me seriously reconsidering where I hold my accounts going forward. I did not expect that a legitimate, easily verifiable transaction would result in days of frozen access and unexplained reversals, and I would like the opportunity to see this resolved properly before I make that decision final. Thank you

complaint_text: RE : Formal Escalation Pattern of Servicer Misconduct, RESPA Violations, and Documented Financial Harm I am filing this complaint because the response provided by XXXX XXXX to CFPB Case XXXX, XXXX was inadequate, non-specific, and failed to address the documented pattern of RESPA violations outlined in my original complaint. I am submitting the attached escalation letter as complete documentation of the violations, financial harm, and relief requested. I do not accept the prior response as an adequate resolution of this matter. '' SECTION 1 : OPENING STATEMENT This document constitutes a formal escalation of previously submitted CFPB complaints against XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX It is submitted in response to the inadequate, non-specific, and in some cases factually inaccurate responses provided by both servicers to prior CFPB complaint submissions. Every claim in this escalation is supported by documented evidence, including recorded phone calls, written correspondence, CFPB complaint submissions, court-issued probate documents, servicer letters, and a complete timeline of events maintained throughout these proceedings. My father, XXXX XXXX, passed away approximately six months prior, on XX/XX/XXXX. I am a Colorado resident remotely managing the affairs of a Florida estate. Throughout these proceedings, I have been recovering from XXXX with a XXXX XXXX XXXX a fact that is relevant to the nature and volume of communications I was required to manage and the standard of care I was owed as a protected borrower under federal law. Under RESPA and the CFPB 's Successor-in-Interest rules, servicers are required to communicate clearly, promptly, and accessibly with protected borrowers a standard neither servicer met. 2.2 Successor-in-Interest Status I was established as Successor-in-Interest to this VA-backed mortgage following the completion of full probate proceedings in the state of Florida. Letters of Administration were issued by the court on XX/XX/XXXX, and submitted to both servicers. Despite this, both servicers repeatedly failed to promptly and properly recognize my legal status, resulting in significant delays, redundant document requests, and the continued pursuit of foreclosure proceedings against the estate. This failure to recognize my Successor-in-Interest status is itself a documented RESPA violation and forms the foundation of every subsequent failure outlined in this escalation. SECTION 3 : TIMELINE OF SERVICER MISCONDUCT The following timeline documents the pattern of delays, redundant requests, impossible conditions, and failures of internal communication that characterize the conduct of both servicers throughout these proceedings : SECTION 4 : INADEQUACY OF RESPONSES AND SPECIFIC VIOLATIONS 4.1 Redundant Document Requests ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41 ) Over the course of these proceedings, I submitted the same documents to XXXX XXXX on eight separate occasions. Each time, XXXX XXXX either claimed documents were not received, requested additional documents not previously identified, or restarted the review process without explanation. This pattern was compounded by two servicing transfers starting on XX/XX/XXXXXXXX from XXXX XXXX to XXXX, and from XXXX to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX during which loan files were either not transferred completely or not reviewed by incoming servicers, resulting in the document submission cycle being restarted each time. Under RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41, a servicer may not request the same documents or information previously submitted by a borrower. XXXX XXXX XXXX pattern of redundant requests constitutes a clear and repeated violation of this provision. 4.2 Failure to Recognize Successor-in-Interest Status ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.38 ) Despite the submission of court-issued Letters of Administration establishing my legal status as Successor-in-Interest, both servicers repeatedly failed to promptly and properly recognize this status. This failure caused direct delays in loss mitigation processing and resulted in foreclosure proceedings being pursued against an estate whose legal representative had been clearly identified and documented. Most egregiously, on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX verbally confirmed my Successor-in-Interest status and denied that same status in writing on the same day. This direct contradiction is preserved in the communications record and constitutes a standalone violation of 12 CFR 1024.38. 4.3 Dual Tracking Violation ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41 ( f ) ) Both servicers simultaneously pursued foreclosure proceedings while an active, approved short sale transaction was in progress. This constitutes dual tracking in direct violation of RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41 ( f ), which prohibits a servicer from moving forward with foreclosure while a complete loss mitigation application is pending. The XX/XX/XXXX, conditional approval with an impossible 15-day deadline and {$0.00} allocated for subordinate lien releases further strengthens this finding a conditional approval designed to fail does not satisfy the dual-tracking prohibition. Furthermore, following the XX/XX/XXXX, closing after payoff funds had been received a Notice of Foreclosure Sale bearing my name and property address was published in the Business Observer on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. These publications occurred because neither the servicer nor the foreclosure attorney filed the required cancellation with the court in a timely manner, constituting a continuation of dual-tracking conduct even after the loss mitigation transaction had successfully closed. 4.4 Failure to Maintain Accurate Internal Records and Communicate with Legal Counsel ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.38 / 12 CFR 1024.40 ) The servicing transfer from XXXX XXXX to XXXX XXXX XXXX occurred while an active short sale transaction was in progress. This transfer resulted in a complete loss of institutional knowledge regarding the history of the loan, the loss mitigation proceedings, and the active short sale offer. The full extent of this failure was revealed at the foreclosure mediation on XX/XX/XXXX. At that mediation, XXXX 's own foreclosure attorney was unaware of the deed-in-lieu attempt, prior efforts to sell the estate, and the all-cash short-sale offer that had been actively maintained since XX/XX/XXXX. It was only through my presentation of the complete case timeline at mediation that XXXX 's legal counsel became informed of the history of this loan placing an extraordinary and wholly inappropriate burden on a Successor-in-Interest who was simultaneously recovering from XXXX with a XXXX XXXX XXXX and managing a Florida estate remotely from Colorado. Twenty days after that mediation on XX/XX/XXXX a conditional short sale approval was issued. Under RESPA 12 CFR 1024.40, servicers are required to maintain continuity of contact and ensure that loss mitigation information is transferred completely and accurately during a servicing transfer. Under RESPA 12 CFR 1024.38, servicers are required to maintain accurate and accessible records and to provide personnel including legal counsel with access to all relevant information. Neither requirement was met. This failure was again repeated when XXXX transferred servicing to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX effective XX/XX/XXXXXXXX again while an active, approved short sale transaction was in progress requiring yet another round of re-establishment of Successor-in-Interest status and loss mitigation history with an incoming servicer. 4.5 Systematic Rejection of All-Cash Short Sale Offers ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41 ) The XX/XX/XXXX, all-cash offer that ultimately closed on XX/XX/XXXX, was not the first all-cash short-sale offer presented; as a minimum, the seventh. An all-cash offer existed as early as XX/XX/XXXX but could not be formally submitted because XXXX XXXX simultaneously required the borrower to pursue a loan modification and hardship affidavit process blocking one loss mitigation path while mandating another. This simultaneous requirement placed the borrower in an impossible position and constitutes a dual-tracking violation under 12 CFR 1024.41 ( f ) independent of the foreclosure dual-tracking violation documented in Section 4.3. At least five additional all-cash short sale offers were subsequently presented. XXXX XXXX either rejected them outright or delayed decisions so long that buyers abandoned the transaction entirely. When the borrower raised concerns about these repeated rejections and delays, XXXX XXXX XXXX response was : " You just do not understand how the process works. '' This response is not only dismissive and condescending it is factually inverted. The borrower understood the process precisely. She had at minimum seven all-cash buyers ready to close. It was the servicer whose delays, rejections, and impossible conditions destroyed six viable all-cash transactions before a seventh buyer extraordinary in their patience and commitment held on for eight months to finally reach closing. Each abandoned transaction represents not only a lost opportunity to resolve the estate but additional months of accruing mortgage arrears, HOA arrears, and foreclosure-related costs all of which were the direct and foreseeable consequence of XXXX XXXX XXXX failure to act on viable offers in a timely manner. This statement also constitutes a violation of 12 CFR 1024.38 ( b ) ( 2 ), which requires servicers to provide accurate information to borrowers in a timely manner. Telling a borrower she does not understand a process that she understood better than the servicer 's own attorney is a documented misrepresentation that caused direct harm it discouraged the borrower from escalating legitimate concerns at a time when earlier escalation might have preserved one or more of the six lost all-cash transactions. 4.6 Impossible Closing Conditions ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.41 ( f ) ) The XX/XX/XXXX, conditional approval letter issued by XXXX imposed a closing deadline of XX/XX/XXXXXXXX just 15 days while simultaneously requiring subordinate lien releases for which {$0.00} had been allocated. Specifically, the HOA subordinate lien which ultimately required negotiation and settlement was identified as a required condition of closing with no funding allocated and no servicer representative assigned to facilitate its resolution. These conditions were mathematically and legally impossible to satisfy within the timeframe given. The practical effect of this approval was to create the appearance of loss mitigation compliance while ensuring the transaction could not close a pattern that mirrors the XX/XX/XXXXXXXX loan modification blockage documented in Section 4.5 and further supports a finding of bad faith loss mitigation conduct. This pattern of issuing approvals with impossible conditions is consistent with the broader pattern of servicer conduct documented throughout these proceedings. 4.7 Judicial Default Against Non-Existent Party ( RESPA 12 CFR 1024.38 ( b ) ( 1 ) ) On XX/XX/XXXX, a judicial default was entered against " Unknown Spouse Of '' a non-existent party with no legal standing in these proceedings. Neither XXXX XXXX nor XXXX XXXX XXXX acknowledged or corrected this error in their CFPB complaint responses. This error reflects the broader failure of both servicers to maintain accurate records and exercise basic due diligence in their legal proceedings against this estate. Servicers are required under 12 CFR 1024.38 ( b ) ( 1 ) to maintain accurate and accessible records of the identity of parties with legal standing. Pursuing judicial action against a non-existent party while simultaneously failing to recognize the documented Successor-in-Interest is a direct and irreconcilable contradiction. This same failure of due diligence in maintaining accurate party records contributed directly to the XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, foreclosure publications in which a Notice of Foreclosure Sale bearing my name and property address was published after the short sale had already closed, because the foreclosure attorney failed to file the Motion to Cancel in a timely manner following the XX/XX/XXXX, closing. On XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, foreclosure publications directly caused unsolicited investor contact, public exposure of my personal information, and emotional distress all occurring AFTER a successful closing that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX had approved on XX/XX/XXXX. This claim arises out of an initial fraudulent charge for XXXX XXXX and some cents on my debit card in early May to a restaurant in XXXX, GA. I have never been to Georgia. I received a call from someone representing themselves to be Navy Federal. They used Navy Federals customer service number XXXX to make this call. I never provided this person with any personal identifying information (SSN, DOB, etc.). This person very clearly had access to my bank account information and went through transactions that I made to verify that I had made those. They were able to see my exact balances in both my checking and savings account that have now been closed. This person also sent text messages pretending to be Navy Federal. Navy Federal as a legitimate institution never alerted me about that initial fraudulent charge. This person then continued to mislead me and state that I was speaking to the fraud department. For the record, the process they used is incredibly similar to Navy Federals legitimate processes. 
I also received texts from another phone number XXXX) to which I was told is an illegitimate phone number, but I was unaware of this. For one my claim should be honored, because this is a security breach of Navy Federals fault. If someone is able to reach customers and use Navy Federals phone number to misrepresent customers, that is the responsibility of the institution. At the minimum, the institution needs to be on top of issues like this and has a duty to inform customers that activity like this is taking place. 
As mentioned, this person who misrepresented themselves as a Navy Federal employee had access to my online bank account. When I first called the legitimate institution the employee I spoke to went through my sign in history. The same way they were able to use Navy Federals customer service number, they also made every sign in appear that it came from my iPhone. I only use the one device (my iPhone) to sign into the mobile banking app. The only thing they did differently was they checked my account statements. I do not ever open those. I only check the transactions tab when reviewing my account history. This person also went in and disabled all of my notifications- texts and emails. After finding this out, I went to Apple and had them do a security check of my devices- both my iPhone and personal MacBook. I do not use my MacBook to sign into my bank accounts, but was worried about a security breach of everything since this was a very complex issue. I had all of my devices restored to their factory settings and checked for any sort of malware, to which there was nothing suspicious on either of them. I have also subsequently changed my passwords for quite literally every single account I have.
Furthermore, my claim should be honored due to the nature of this activity. Never in my years of being a Navy Federal Member have I made transactions this large multiple times a month. The largest purchases I make are my rent and student loan payments. I am especially disheartened with this activity as I just started a new job and was able to even save that amount of money. It was the first time in my life even had that amount of money that I wrongfully thought was safe in my Navy Federal account. Additionally, you can see through my banking history I have never made purchases of this kind. I have used XXXX XXXX a couple of times in the past but did not have my bank account linked to it. I have never used XXXX XXXX or Banxa. After this event is resolved, I will no longer be using any sort of third party app or P2P services. I am even weary of XXXX since these individuals attempted to XXXX themselves through my bank account. I had no way to know that Navy Federal was not the entity contacting me when they used the institutions phone number so that is not my fault. I should also be notified of unusual sign ins to my account.
 It is also on Navy Federal to alert customers of any emerging scams and data breaches that have the potential to pose widespread risk to their customers. It also a duty on a bank to protect and ensure the confidentiality of consumer data and I believe this duty was breached as someone was able to access all of my account information to no fault of my own. I have never shared my Navy Federal Account information, passwords, or any personal identifying information with any other third party. 
I understand the federal laws surrounding this investigation. I also believe Navy Federal did not fully investigate this matter the first time my claims were denied. For XXXX, everyone has continued to get the amount in dispute incorrect. XXXX, this investigation was complete in approximately two business days. I went in person to file the transaction paperwork to expedite the process and all claims were denied on XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX, I received no documentation whatsoever as to why my claims were denied. I was merely informed that the information I provided contradicts claims of unauthorized activity. Finally, while I understand there has been confusion about the amount in question all bank records (incorrectly) have the amount in question at over XXXX At that point, the institution has a duty under federal law to document and report these suspected financial crimes. I am very disgruntled with Navy Federals sincere lack of help and attention to this matter. 
I have called countless times once I realized I was misled. Several times, I have been referred to the fraud department and left on hold for over an hour. For example, last XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I attempted to call back as it is my goal to get this resolved as quickly as possible and I was left on hold for over an hour and a half. This has happened multiple times. I understand the high workload of bank employees, but the way this keeps happening gives the illusion that the institution just hopes I hang up. Maybe XXXX or XXXX people during this entire process have actually helped me. Just as a note, the people who misrepresented themselves as Navy Federal also used the same prolonged hold times and hold music. I do not make enough money to just let this go, especially since this was not my fault. They copied the entire phone process of Navy Federal identically. I hope you take this seriously, as this has severe consequences for both the institution and entire customer base. 
Navy Federal believes I authorized this fraud and that is not correct. I understand the resolution of my claims turns on whether this was authorized or unauthorized fraud. Authorization requires a knowing and intentional decision to transfer funds to the actual recipient of the transaction. Since I was misrepresented, I did not consent to any of the transactions made through my account and thus did not authorize this activity. I did not knowingly authorize the transfers in question. This was more than just a scam. My apparent authorization was induced by someone who falsely represented themselves as Navy Federal Credit Union, used Navy Federals actual telephone number through caller-ID spoofing or related means, and possessed detailed account information that made this misrepresentation appear credible and would lead a reasonable customer to believe they were communicating with authorized Bank personnel. As mentioned, they used the same processes as Navy Federal- using the same voice system (for example, the one that says based off your phone number, it appears you are a member). 
Authorization requires a knowing and voluntary instruction by the account holder. Because my alleged participation in these transactions was obtained through material misrepresentation about the identity and authority of the person directing the transaction, any participation on my part was not informed or voluntary authorization. I believed I was following instructions from the bank itself to protect my accounts from further fraud. Therefore, these transactions should be treated as unauthorized fraud losses rather than legitimate customer-authorized transfers.
At all times, I believed I was acting pursuant to instructions by Navy Federal for the purpose of protecting my accounts from fraud and getting my money back. I know for purposes of authorized transactions you do not care about my intent. However, I did not intend to transfer money to anyone, to relinquish control of my money, or confer any benefit upon the people who represented themselves as Navy Federal. My intent was solely to follow what I reasonably understood to be legitimate security procedures.
The perpetrators informed me that fraudulent activity occurred in my accounts and instructed me that certain actions were necessary to reverse, stop, and protect against unauthorized transactions. Acting in reliance on those representations I followed what I believed to be Navy Federals fraud prevention procedures. I was specifically told the transactions were a part of Navy Federals fraud resolution process. My objective was not to send money to another person. Instead it was to follow Navy Federals instructions to get my hard-earned money back.
The fraud succeeded because the perpetrators induced my actions by falsely assuming Navy Federals identity and exploiting my confidential account information. Any apparent authorization was therefore vitiated by fraud. Consent obtained through material deception or misrepresentation is not legally effective consent. A transaction cannot be deemed authorized merely because a customer aided in the steps necessary to conduct the transaction when those steps were undertaken in reliance upon fraudulent representations concerning the identity, authority, and purpose of the party directing the transactions. 
Moreover, the circumstances of this fraud raise serious questions regarding account security. As mentioned several times, the perpetrators possessed detailed account information and successfully impersonated Navy Federal, such that a reasonable customer would be convinced the communications were genuine. This loss was not caused by a voluntary decision to send money to known third party; it was caused by a sophisticated impersonation scheme that depended on the misuse of Navy Federals identity and my confidential account information. During the first call I made to report this upon finding out I was misrepresented, the Navy Federal employee stated something along the lines of its okay, these people play on your emotions. I would also like to clear that up. No emotions were involved in this, there was no scam story to induce this, it appeared strictly business under Navy Federals exact processes. This person knew non-public account information: all my recent transactions, balances, account numbers, the addresses affiliated with my account. They even knew I recently changed my billing address. These facts alone prove this was not merely some random scam call After this experience, I honestly do not have confidence in Navy Federals security practices especially since someone was able to make all of the sign ins to my account look like they came from my device. 
Navy Federals own identity, reputation, telephone number, and confidential account information were essential tools used to carry out this scheme. The unauthorized fraud succeeded precisely because the perpetrators convincingly presented themselves as Navy Federal and possessed information to lead a reasonable customer to trust their instructions. Under these circumstances, characterizing the transactions as authorized elevates form over substance and ignores the reality that the transactions were the direct product of sophisticated bank impersonation fraud.
In conclusion, the relevant question is whether I knowingly authorized the transfers in question to the perpetrators (criminals who represented themselves as Navy Federal Credit Union). I did not. I believed I was communicating with and acting under the direction of the Bank itself. Because my actions were induced by fraud and material misrepresentation, the transactions were not genuinely authorized and should be treated as unauthorized fraudulent transfers for which reimbursement is required. To hold otherwise would improperly equate fraudulently induced conduct with informed authorization and would shift the entire risk of sophisticated bank-impersonation fraud onto customers who reasonably rely upon Navy Federals identity, telephone systems, and account-security representations.

complaint_text: ESCROW ACCOUNT XXXX Property Address XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, CA XXXX I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of my mortgage escrow ( impound ) account removal request and the inconsistent and conflicting information I have received from Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing. I closed escrow on my home purchase on XX/XX/year>. Prior to closing, I requested that the escrow ( impound ) account be removed. My loan XXXX, XXXX XXXX of XXXX Bank, was aware of this request before closing. After closing, my mortgage servicing was transferred to Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing. When my first mortgage payment became due on XX/XX/year>, I discovered that my mortgage payment included escrow ( impound ) charges despite my prior request to remove them. I contacted Shellpoint and was informed that my previous lender would need to submit the request in writing and that I would also need to provide a signed letter requesting removal of the escrow account. I complied with this request. In addition, XXXX XXXX emailed Shellpoint on XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX regarding the escrow removal request and provided me with a screenshot showing that the email had been sent. I contacted Shellpoint the following day to confirm receipt and was informed over the phone that the escrow account would be removed within XXXX to XXXX business days. However, I then received a letter dated XX/XX/year>, stating that my request had been denied because " the loan does not meet servicing requirements for escrow account deletion. '' On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX, I spoke with Shellpoint representative XXXX XXXX to obtain a status update. She informed me that there was no record of any escrow removal request in their system and that I would need to submit a new request. I explained that I had already submitted the request, provided the relevant dates, and advised her that my prior lender had also submitted documentation. She stated that no such information could be found in their records and further advised that my previous lender could not request escrow removal on my behalf. I then requested that Shellpoint submit the removal request. To verify that the request had been submitted, I called Shellpoint again on XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX and spoke with representative XXXX XXXX She informed me that no new request had been submitted and that my request had already been denied. When I asked what requirements applied to escrow removal, she stated that I would need to wait XXXX years before the escrow account could be removed. This was the first time I had ever been informed of a purported two-year requirement. I was not provided with any documentation identifying such a requirement, and I do not recall signing any document agreeing to maintain an escrow account for XXXX years. Throughout this process, I have received conflicting and inconsistent information from Shellpoint representatives. Some representatives have stated that no request exists, others have stated that the request was denied, and another representative advised that the escrow account would be removed within XXXX to XXXX business days. I have also not received confirmation that my most recent request was submitted or reviewed. I am current on my mortgage payments. I am not delinquent. My homeowner 's insurance is active and paid. I have made repeated good-faith efforts to understand the requirements and process for escrow removal, but I have been unable to obtain consistent information or a clear explanation regarding the denial. I am requesting that Shellpoint : Provide a complete written explanation of the specific contractual, investor, or servicing requirements that allegedly prevent removal of the escrow account. Provide copies of any documents that require me to maintain escrow for a specified period, including any alleged two-year requirement. Confirm whether my prior escrow removal requests were received and reviewed. Conduct a formal review of my eligibility for escrow account removal. Correct any servicing errors and provide a written response explaining the status of my request. I appreciate the CFPB XXXX assistance in helping obtain a clear and accurate response regarding this matter. -XXXX XXXX XXXX & XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

complaint_text: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Consumer Complaint Subject : Systemic Escrow Mismanagement, Unauthorized Funds Siphoning, Intentional FCRA Reporting Violations, and Illegal Refusal to Recognize a Deceased Borrower Status / Successor in Interest Respondent : Freedom Mortgage Corporation Associated Loan Number : XXXX I. Executive Summary This complaint is filed to formalize a severe, multi-year pattern of systemic administrative failures, gross escrow mismanagement, malicious credit reporting violations, and weaponized corporate incompetence by Freedom Mortgage Corporation. Over consecutive years, Freedom Mortgage has systematically abandoned its fiduciary obligations as an escrow-holding loan servicer. The servicer has failed to timely and fully disburse local property taxes and property insurance premiums, while simultaneously issuing unauthorized, unverified disbursements out of the consumers escrow account. Furthermore, Freedom Mortgage is engaging in a flagrant, multi-layered trap designed to ruin the consumer 's credit standing and prevent them from exiting this loan. The company has weaponized its own approved emergency disaster forbearance to manufacture a legal fiction of delinquency, intentionally misreported a current account as " 30+ days late '' to the credit bureaus, and flatly refused to remove deceased co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX from the loan despite the official submission of her death certificate. When notified of these critical errors via statutory Notices of Error ( NOEs ), Qualified Written Requests ( QWRs ), and internal portal messages, Freedom Mortgage engaged in bad-faith evasion, circular delays, and adversarial customer service. The servicer is actively wielding its own manufactured errors to lock the consumer into an toxic loan structure to maximize its own interest revenue. This predatory corporate paradigm has exacted a profound and quantifiable toll on the consumer 's health, XXXX management, and financial well-being. II. Factual Chronology and Combined Escrow Violations 1. The XXXX Property Tax Failure and Notice of Error As verified in the document " freedom notice of error.pdf '', on XX/XX/XXXX, the consumer, XXXX XXXX, issued a formal statutory Notice of Error ( NOE ) to Freedom Mortgage. The consumer had received an explicit alert from the XXXX XXXX Tax Commissioner stating that a Fieri Facias ( FiFa )/ Tax Lien would be issued against the real property ( located at XXXX XXXX XXXX ) due to unremitted XXXX property taxes. Despite the consumers escrow account showing " Tax Disbursements '' ( including a deduction of {$350.00} on XX/XX/XXXX ), Freedom Mortgage mismanaged the escrow resources, failed to pay the complete billed amount of {$830.00}, and left a delinquent balance of {$350.00} to accrue interest, fees, and penalties. The consumers XXXX explicitly demanded that Freedom Mortgage correct this mismanagement, protect the property from the impending lien, and ensure no fees or interest were assessed to the consumers account. As documented in the file " image.png '', the consumer followed up with Freedom Mortgage regarding the official Lien for FIERI FACIAS recorded on XX/XX/XXXX, in Book XXXX, Page XXXX of Official Records in favor of the City of XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Customer Care issued a response that encapsulates bad-faith evasion : " Please be advised that, upon reviewing your request, Freedom Mortgage is unable to assist you, as the lien referenced in your question is not held by us ; it is held by the City of XXXX. Therefore, we recommend that you directly contact XXXXhe County for further assistance and clarification. '' Freedom Mortgage bypassed the underlying truth : the lien was held by the XXXX of XXXX exclusively because Freedom Mortgage failed to fulfill its statutory obligation to pay the property taxes out of the consumer 's funded escrow account. 2. The Homeowners Insurance Sabotage and Predatory Force-Placed Premium The servicers malicious patterns are further laid bare by a dual-document timeline involving the consumer 's hazard insurance : The Insurance Non-Payment Notice : As verified in the file " XXXX '', the consumers hazard insurance carrier, XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ) , issued an urgent status notice for policy XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX regarding mortgage loan XXXX for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX explicitly stated that because Freedom Mortgage failed to collect and remit insurance premiums, XXXX was forced to switch to billing the consumer directly for a balance of {$3000.00}. The Calculated Force-Placed Notice : As verified in the file " XXXX '', on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Mortgage issued a notice to the consumer stating they had force-placed an unnecessary, expensive insurance policy onto the account costing {$2400.00} annually, fraudulently citing a " lack of insurance information. '' This is a textbook example of a predatory servicer trap. Freedom Mortgage defaulted on its obligation to disburse the consumers XXXX hazard insurance premium out of the escrow account, which forced XXXX to drop the mortgage-billing arrangement. Then, Freedom Mortgage weaponized its own failure to pay the existing carrier by fabricating a " lack of insurance information '' to force-place a costly duplicate policy onto the account. 3. Unsubstantiated and Unauthorized Escrow Siphoning The weaponized incompetence of Freedom Mortgage is further demonstrated by completely unauthorized and unverified withdrawals from the consumer 's escrow balance. As documented in " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage issued a " Tax and Insurance Disbursement Confirmation '' for the account ending in XXXX. The confirmation notes that a payment was completed on XX/XX/XXXX to XXXX XXXX XXXX in the amount of {$420.00} for a " XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX The consumer has absolutely no knowledge of this disbursement, has received no prior notice or breakdown as to why it was paid, and has never been provided proof of a valid lien associated with this payment by Freedom Mortgage. Freedom Mortgage simply withdrew consumer funds to pay an unverified municipal charge, completely violating basic accounting, verification, and escrow standards. 4. Illegal Refusal to Acknowledge Deceased Status & Successor Options The most egregious display of continuous administrative bad faith is Freedom Mortgage 's complete refusal to update the account following the passing of co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX. The consumer has formally provided and proven through the portal that XXXX XXXX XXXX is deceased by submitting her official death certificate. Despite receiving undeniable legal documentation of her passing, Freedom Mortgage flatly refuses to remove her name from the loan account, refuses to update the loan data fields, and completely ignores requests to provide the legally required Successor in Interest packets, confirmation tracks, or assumptions paths. By pretending a deceased individual is still active while ignoring the living borrower, Freedom Mortgage actively cuts off the legal avenues necessary to modify, restructure, or clean up the loan terms. 5. Weaponized Forbearance, Payment Rollover, and False Credit Reporting A review of files " XXXX '' through " XXXX '' exposes a malicious credit-destroying scheme orchestrated by Freedom Mortgage post-forbearance. The Approved Forbearance : As verified in " XXXX '', on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom Mortgage formally approved an emergency disaster Forbearance Plan for the consumer 's loan ( XXXX ), which temporarily suspended monthly mortgage payments from XX/XX/XXXX, through XX/XX/XXXX. The Payment Application Trajectory : As verified in internal messages ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ) and a letter from Supervisor XXXX XXXX ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ), the forbearance period actually remained active from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. During this entire time, the consumer consistently resumed making monthly payments via XXXX. As shown in " XXXX '', an AutoPay payment of {$1200.00} was successfully processed with confirmation XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. The Rolling Delinquency Fraud : In " XXXX '', " XXXX '', and " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage admits in writing that because no payment was made in XX/XX/XXXX ( the exact month covered by their own approved disaster forbearance ), every payment after [ that ] has been applied to the prior month. The Fraudulent Bureau Reporting : Because Freedom Mortgage backward-rolled every single timely post-forbearance payment to the prior month, they created a permanent, artificial one-month lag. They then weaponized this internal accounting fiction to report the consumer to the credit bureaus as " 30 days late '' for XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. As proven by the official credit bureau dispute report in " XXXX '', Freedom Mortgage verified this devastating derogatory remark as " accurate '' to the bureaus on XX/XX/XXXX, showing an active " 30 '' day delinquency rating for XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. As the consumer detailed in formal portal disputes ( " XXXX '' and " XXXX '' ) and a executive escalation to Freedom Mortgage XXXX XXXX XXXX ( " XXXX '' ), this practice is completely fraudulent. If a payment was legitimately missing from XXXX, it was legally mandated to be handled within the forbearance framework or reported late in XXXX is an explicit violation of federal law to report a consumer as delinquent in XXXX for a payment that was fully and timely processed on XX/XX/XXXX. III. Statutory Violations and Relevant Legal Precedents Freedom Mortgage 's continuous actions constitute explicit, actionable violations of federal and state consumer protection laws : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) & ( b ) ) : Furnishers are strictly prohibited from reporting information that is inaccurate or materially misleading. Under 1681s-2 ( b ), upon receipt of a dispute, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and delete or correct inaccurate data. Freedom Mortgage willfully verified a patently false " XX/XX/XXXX Delinquency '' to the bureaus despite having processed the consumer 's payment on XX/XX/XXXX. CARES Act & CFPB Bulletin XXXX ( Forbearance Credit Reporting ) : Federal law mandates that if a borrower is granted a forbearance accommodation and resumes payments as scheduled, the servicer must report the account as current. Rolling payments backward to force an artificial delinquency post-forbearance directly subverts the CARES Act. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) / Regulation X ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.17 ( k ) & 1024.30-.41 ) : Freedom Mortgage violated 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( g ) by failing to timely disburse escrow property taxes and XXXX insurance premiums. They additionally violated federal Successor in Interest rules by failing to establish transparent communication tracks, update account records, or provide assumption paths to XXXX XXXX after receiving formal portal notification of co-borrower XXXX XXXX XXXX ' death. Illegal Assessment of Force-Placed Insurance ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.37 ) : Servicers are prohibited from force-placing hazard insurance unless they have a reasonable basis to believe a borrower 's coverage has lapsed. XXXX has no basis ; the premium breakdown was caused entirely by their own failure to pay XXXX out of the escrow account. Binding Case Law & Enforcement History : 1. Federal Precedent ( XXXX XXXX Freedom Mortgage Corp., XXXX XXXX XXXX ) : Reaffirmed that under RESPA ( 12 U.S.C . 2605 ( g ) ), the obligation to make timely escrow payments is strict, and Freedom Mortgage can not bypass its statutory liabilities when escrowed funds are neglected. 2. Recent Systemic Litigation : Freedom Mortgage faces active litigation for this exact combination of predatory behavior. In XXXX XXXX Freedom Mortgage Corporation ( XXXX. XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ), the servicer was sued for botched escrow calculations and illegally force-placing duplicate hazard insurance overcharges. 3. Documented Regulatory Recidivism : In XX/XX/XXXX, the CFPB penalized Freedom Mortgage Corporation {$3.00} XXXX, with Director XXXX XXXX explicitly labeling them a " repeat offender '' that systemically ignores compliance orders and handles " error-riddled mortgage data. '' Furthermore, in XX/XX/XXXX, the New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs executed a {$500000.00} Consent Order against Freedom Mortgage for violating the Consumer Fraud Act ( CFA ) by failing to timely disburse escrow payments and providing deceptive information to borrowers. Freedom relocated its corporate headquarters from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX, XXXX in the midst of these expanding regulatory investigations into their servicing mechanics. IV. Quantifiable Financial Harm and Impact on Well-Being The Escrow Trap to Enforce Poverty : By mismanaging escrow disbursements, creating artificial title clouds ( the recorded FiFa lien ) , siphoning unverified funds ( {$420.00} municipal withdrawal ) without documentation, fabricating thousand-dollar force-placed insurance charges, ignoring a legal death certificate to freeze the loan 's status, and obliterating the consumer 's credit score via fraudulent " 30-day late '' trended data reporting, Freedom Mortgage has engineered a total financial chokehold. Because a property with an active tax lien, erratic escrow shortages, or locked title status can not satisfy standard underwriting guidelines, Freedom Mortgage uses its own administrative failures to trap the consumer in this loan. This completely blocks the consumer from refinancing into better market terms or exiting the loan, preserving Freedom Mortgage 's interest revenue while systematically keeping the consumer financially suppressed. Profound Health and Emotional Damage : The psychological cost of experiencing years of weaponized corporate incompetence can not be overstated. Constantly defending one 's home against tax foreclosure, fighting circular bureaucratic loops, tracking down unauthorized withdrawals, navigating the emotional toll of a co-borrower 's passing while the servicer uses her death as a bureaucratic stalling tool, and managing severe health XXXX under an environment of constant corporate gaslighting has inflicted a severe, compounding toll on the consumer 's physical and mental health. The chronic stress of dealing with an adversarial institution that actively sabotages your credit and financial health has drastically deteriorated the consumers daily quality of life.

I have raised versions of these issues before and been told " no error occurred, '' but the servicer 's own documents contradict that determination, and I can now prove it with a line-by-line reconciliation ( attached ). UNANSWERED QUALIFIED WRITTEN REQUEST. I submitted a QWR/Notice of Error on XX/XX/XXXX ( Ref # XXXX ). The servicer acknowledged receipt and set its own extended response deadline of XX/XX/XXXX under 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( e ) ( 3 ). That deadline passed with no substantive written response. This is a violation of RESPA Section 2605 ( e ) and Regulation X Section 1024.35 ( e ). PAYMENT MISAPPLICATION DOCUMENTED BY THE SERVICER 'S OWN LEDGER. I reconciled the servicer 's internal " MRC Payment Activity '' export against my monthly statements and my XXXX XXXX records. Of roughly 30 months reviewed, 19 show confirmed conflicts, including a XX/XX/XXXX payment the servicer 's own written response denies receiving, which my bank confirms cleared on retry ( Ref XXXX ). My bank records also show a clean, dated behavioral break in XX/XX/XXXX : payments that had cleared on a single attempt every month for years began failing and requiring retries, coinciding exactly with the servicer 's payment increase and an escrow shortage it had created. The servicer 's own XX/XX/XXXX Research Letter ( Ref # XXXX ) attributes reversals to " insufficient funds and invalid account number, '' despite the same account having drafted successfully for over XXXX years with no explanation given for why the account number became invalid. ESCROW MISMANAGEMENT TRACED TO A SINGLE ROOT CAUSE. The HUD Handbook also states that during the month in which a Forbearance Agreement expires, the mortgagee must determine whether the borrower qualifies for : an additional Forbearance period ; a Repayment Plan ; or a permanent Loss Mitigation Option. This HUD language demonstrates that Forbearance and Permanent Loss Mitigation Options are separate FHA loss mitigation options with separate eligibility requirements. CITIBANK, N.A.,XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXPlaintiff XXXX XXXX XXXX"Plaintiff" or "XXXX XXXX appearing pro se, brings this Complaint against Defendant Citibank, N.A. ("Citibank" or "Defendant"), and alleges as follows:

NATURE OF THE ACTION
1. This is a consumer protection action arising from Defendant Citibank, N.A.'s unlawful handling of a billing dispute under the Fair Credit Billing Act, Truth in Lending Act, Consumer Financial Protection Act, and Fair Credit Reporting Act, and related New York State law claims.
2. On XXXX XXXX XXXX an unauthorized charge of $XXXX was posted to Plaintiff's Citibank credit card account by a merchant identified as XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX" located in XXXX, New York. Plaintiff never authorized this charge.
3. Plaintiff timely disputed the charge. Citibank opened a dispute case, issued a provisional credit, and requested additional documentation. Plaintiff fully cooperated, providing all requested information and confirming that the charge was unauthorized and that the merchant was wholly unresponsive.
4. Despite Plaintiff's full cooperation and the complete absence of any evidence of authorization, Citibank denied the dispute twice based on a legally fabricated evidentiary standard requiring Plaintiff to prove "the merchant was paid by another means." No such standard exists under federal law.
5. Citibank further threatened to report the disputed, unauthorized charge to XXXX XXXX and XXXX, in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
6. Plaintiff brings this action to recover actual damages, statutory damages, punitive damages, and attorney's fees and costs, and to obtain injunctive and declaratory relief.
JURISDICTION AND VENUE
7. Federal Question Jurisdiction. This Court has subject matter jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1331 because this action arises under the laws of the United States, including the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA), 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq.; the Truth in Lending Act (TILA), 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13; the Consumer Financial Protection Act (CFPA), 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536; and the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.
8. Supplemental Jurisdiction. This Court has supplemental jurisdiction over Plaintiff's New York State law claims pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1367(a), as those claims are so related to the federal claims that they form part of the same case or controversy.
9. Venue. Venue is proper in this District pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1391(b) because a substantial part of the events and omissions giving rise to the claims occurred in this District; Citibank, N.A. maintains its principal place of business and legal department at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX New York XXXX, within this District; and Citibank's registered agent for service of legal process, XXXX XXXX XXXX is located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, New York XXXX, within this District.
PARTIES
10. Plaintiff XXXX XXXX is an individual residing at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX New York XXXX. At all relevant times, XXXX XXXX was a cardholder and consumer as defined under the FCBA, TILA, FCRA, and CFPA.
11. Defendant Citibank, N.A. is a national banking association chartered and regulated under the laws of the United States. Citibank maintains its principal operations and legal department at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, New York XXXX. Citibank is a "creditor" and "card issuer" as defined under the FCBA and TILA, a "furnisher of information" as defined under the FCRA, and a "covered person" as defined under the CFPA. Citibank is also registered to do business in the State of New York.
FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
A. The Unauthorized Charge
12. On XXXX XXXX XXXX an unauthorized charge in the amount of $XXXX was posted to XXXX XXXX Citibank credit card account (Account No. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX by a merchant identified as "XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX New York.
13. XXXX XXXX did not authorize, approve, initiate, or benefit from this charge in any way. He had no prior relationship with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and received no goods or services in connection with the transaction.
14. XXXX XXXX attempted to contact the merchant to resolve the matter directly. All such attempts were met with complete non-response.
B. The Dispute and Provisional Credit
15. XXXX XXXX immediately contacted Citibank to dispute the unauthorized charge. Citibank opened Case ID XXXX and issued a provisional credit to XXXX XXXXs account while it purported to investigate.
16. Citibank requested additional documentation from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX fully and timely complied with all requests, providing detailed information confirming that the charge was unauthorized and that the merchant had failed to respond to his outreach.
C. Citibank's Unlawful Denial
17. Notwithstanding XXXX XXXX complete cooperation and the total absence of any evidence of authorization, Citibank reversed the provisional credit and denied the dispute.
18. By letter dated XXXX XXXX XXXX Citibank denied the dispute a second time, asserting that XXXX XXXX documentation failed to prove "the merchant was paid by another means."
19. The evidentiary standard applied by Citibank requiring a cardholder to prove that a merchant was paid by alternative means has no basis in the Fair Credit Billing Act, Regulation Z, or any other applicable federal or state law. It is a fabricated, internally-created standard designed to improperly shift the burden of proof to the consumer.
20. The sole legally relevant question under the FCBA is whether a charge was authorized by the cardholder. The charge was not authorized. Citibank produced no evidence of authorization no signed receipt, no authorization log, no transaction record, no electronic data of any kind.
21. In the XXXX XXXX XXXX denial letter, Citibank also threatened to report XXXX XXXX account to the consumer reporting agencies XXXX XXXX, and XXXX in connection with the disputed, unauthorized charge.
CLAIMS FOR RELIEF
COUNT I Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA) 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq.
22. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
23. The FCBA requires a card issuer, upon receipt of a billing error notice, to conduct a reasonable investigation and either correct the billing error or provide the cardholder with a written explanation setting forth the reasons for the card issuer's belief that the billing statement was correct.
24. The unauthorized charge of $XXXX constitutes a "billing error" as defined in 15 U.S.C. 1666(b), specifically as a charge for property or services not accepted by the obligor or not delivered to the obligor as agreed.
25. Citibank failed to conduct a reasonable investigation. Citibank denied XXXX XXXX dispute without obtaining, producing, or relying upon any competent evidence of authorization no signed receipt, no authorization record, no point-of-sale data, no electronic authorization record, and no evidence whatsoever that XXXX XXXX authorized or benefited from the charge.
26. Citibank's denial was based on a legally fabricated standard requiring Plaintiff to prove payment by alternative means a standard that does not exist under the FCBA.
27. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's violations of the FCBA, Plaintiff has suffered actual damages including the $XXXX charge, associated interest and fees, damage to his credit, and emotional XXXX.
28. Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1640, Plaintiff is entitled to actual damages, statutory damages, and attorney's fees and costs.
COUNT II Truth in Lending Act (TILA) and Regulation Z 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.; 12 C.F.R. 1026.13
29. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
30. Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13, establishes mandatory procedural protections for consumers who dispute billing errors, including specific requirements governing the card issuer's investigation, notification obligations, and the handling of provisional credits.
31. Citibank violated Regulation Z by: (a) failing to properly notify Plaintiff of documentation requirements in a lawful and complete manner; (b) applying an unlawful evidentiary standard to deny the dispute; and (c) improperly reversing the provisional credit in the absence of any competent evidence of authorization, in violation of 12 C.F.R. 1026.13.
32. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's violations of TILA and Regulation Z, Plaintiff has suffered actual damages and is entitled to statutory damages, actual damages, and attorney's fees and costs pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1640.
COUNT III Consumer Financial Protection Act UDAAP 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536
33. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
34. Citibank is a "covered person" within the meaning of 12 U.S.C. 5481(6). The CFPA prohibits covered persons from engaging in any unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice in connection with any consumer financial product or service.
35. Deceptive: Citibank represented to Plaintiff and to cardholders generally that unauthorized charges would be investigated and resolved in accordance with applicable law. Citibank's actual conduct applying a fabricated evidentiary standard to deny valid unauthorized charge disputes materially contradicts those representations and is likely to mislead reasonable consumers.
36. Unfair: Citibank's denial of XXXX XXXX valid dispute causes substantial injury to consumers, is not reasonably avoidable by consumers, and is not outweighed by any countervailing benefit to consumers or competition.
37. Abusive: Citibank took unreasonable advantage of Plaintiff's inability to effectively protect his own interests by inventing a legally non-existent burden of proof and threatening adverse credit reporting for a charge that Plaintiff never authorized.
38. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's UDAAP violations, Plaintiff has suffered actual damages. Plaintiff seeks all available relief including actual damages, restitution, and injunctive relief.
COUNT IV Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.
39. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
40. Citibank is a "furnisher of information" to consumer reporting agencies within the meaning of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2.
41. In its XXXX XXXX XXXX letter, Citibank expressly threatened to report XXXX XXXX account to XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX in connection with the disputed, unauthorized charge of $XXXX.
42. The reporting or threatened reporting of information that Citibank knows or should know is inaccurate specifically, that XXXX XXXX owes a debt for a charge he never authorized and that is the subject of a pending dispute constitutes a violation of the FCRA's accuracy and dispute requirements.
43. Citibank's willful and/or negligent failure to conduct a proper investigation before threatening adverse credit reporting, and its intent to report inaccurate information in connection with a disputed unauthorized charge, violates 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2(a) and 1681n/o.
44. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's FCRA violations, Plaintiff has suffered actual damages including damage to his creditworthiness, emotional distress, and reputational harm, and is entitled to actual damages, statutory damages, punitive damages, and attorney's fees and costs pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o.
COUNT V New York General Business Law 349 Deceptive Acts and Practices
45. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
46. New York General Business Law 349 prohibits deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any business, trade, or commerce in the State of New York.
47. Citibank's conduct applying a legally fabricated evidentiary standard to deny consumer billing disputes in New York, and threatening adverse credit reporting for charges that consumers never authorized constitutes consumer-oriented conduct that is materially misleading and has a broad impact on consumers at large.
48. Plaintiff suffered actual injury as a result of Citibank's deceptive acts and practices, including the loss of $XXXX, credit damage, and emotional XXXX.
49. Pursuant to GBL 349(h), Plaintiff is entitled to actual damages or $XXXX minimum statutory damages per violation, whichever is greater, treble damages up to $XXXX, and attorney's fees.
COUNT VI New York General Business Law 350 False Advertising
50. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
51. New York General Business Law 350 prohibits false advertising in the conduct of any business in the State of New York.
52. Citibank advertises and represents to prospective and existing cardholders, including in its cardholder agreements and marketing materials, that cardholders are protected against unauthorized charges and that Citibank will investigate and resolve such disputes in accordance with applicable law.
53. These representations are false and misleading in light of Citibank's actual practice of denying valid unauthorized charge disputes using fabricated evidentiary standards, as demonstrated by its treatment of XXXX XXXX54. Plaintiff suffered actual injury as a result of Citibank's false advertising and is entitled to the remedies provided under GBL 350-e.
COUNT VII Breach of Contract
55. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
56. Plaintiff and Citibank are parties to a valid and binding cardholder agreement governing the use of XXXX XXXX credit card account.
57. The cardholder agreement obligates Citibank to investigate billing disputes and to resolve unauthorized charge disputes in good faith and in accordance with applicable law.
58. Citibank materially breached the cardholder agreement by: (a) failing to conduct a reasonable or good faith investigation of XXXX XXXX dispute; (b) denying the dispute based on a legally non-existent evidentiary standard; (c) reversing the provisional credit without competent evidence of authorization; and (d) threatening to report inaccurate information to consumer reporting agencies in connection with an unauthorized charge.
59. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's breach of contract, Plaintiff has suffered actual damages in an amount to be proven at trial, including the unauthorized charge of $XXXX, associated interest and fees, and consequential damages.
COUNT VIII Common Law Negligence
60. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.
61. Citibank owed Plaintiff a duty of reasonable care in the investigation and resolution of billing disputes, including the duty to obtain competent evidence before denying a consumer's claim of an unauthorized charge.
62. Citibank breached this duty by failing to conduct even a minimally competent investigation, by applying a fabricated standard of proof, by denying the dispute in the complete absence of any authorization evidence, and by threatening adverse credit reporting for an unverified, disputed, unauthorized charge.
63. As a direct and proximate result of Citibank's negligence, Plaintiff suffered actual damages including the unauthorized charge of $XXXX, associated fees, credit damage, and emotional XXXX.
PRAYER FOR RELIEF
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff XXXX XXXX respectfully requests that this Court enter judgment against Defendant Citibank, N.A. as follows:
	An order requiring Citibank to permanently reverse and credit the unauthorized charge of $XXXX, plus all accrued interest and fees associated therewith;
	Actual damages in an amount to be proven at trial;
	Statutory damages pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1640 (FCBA/TILA), 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o (FCRA), and New York General Business Law 349;
	Punitive damages as authorized by applicable law;
	An injunction requiring Citibank to immediately rescind any adverse credit reporting made or threatened against Plaintiff's account in connection with this dispute;
	An injunction requiring Citibank to reopen and lawfully reinvestigate Case ID XXXX in accordance with the FCBA and Regulation Z;
	Declaratory relief stating that Citibank's application of a "paid by another means" evidentiary standard in billing disputes violates the FCBA and constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice under the CFPA;
	Reasonable attorney's fees and costs pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1640, 15 U.S.C. 1681n/o, New York GBL 349, and all other applicable law;
	Pre-judgment and post-judgment interest as permitted by law; and
	Such other and further relief as this Court deems just and proper.


Respectfully submitted,

/s/ XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX New York XXXX'

complaint_text: I strongly disagree with PennyMacs decision to continue reporting the 30-day late payment without considering the full circumstances of my account. I did not ignore my mortgage obligations. When I experienced financial hardship, I contacted PennyMac to seek assistance and entered into a forbearance plan in good faith. At every stage, I acted responsibly and worked with your company to resolve my account. Once I was able, I brought my loan current and fulfilled my obligations. While PennyMac claims the reporting is technically accurate, accuracy alone does not end the inquiry. Mortgage servicers have the ability to make goodwill adjustments when warranted, particularly where a borrower has demonstrated good faith, resolved the delinquency, and has not engaged in a pattern of irresponsible payment behavior. Your refusal to consider the extraordinary circumstances surrounding my hardship is unreasonable and results in continued damage to my credit despite my efforts to work with your company. Reporting this isolated late payment undermines the purpose of loss mitigation programs, which are intended to help borrowers recover from temporary financial hardshipnot to leave them with long-term credit damage after they have successfully brought their loan current. I request that PennyMac immediately conduct a meaningful review of my account rather than relying on a generic statement that the reporting was accurate. I also request that PennyMac exercise its discretion to remove the 30-day late payment as a goodwill adjustment. If PennyMac continues to deny this request without fully considering the facts and my payment history, I will continue pursuing all available avenues for review through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and any other appropriate regulatory agencies. I expect a substantive response that specifically addresses the circumstances of my case rather than a form response repeating that the reporting was accurate.
